name: DNA code A4GC(9,6)
description: Find as many DNA words of length 9 as possible, that is, strings over the letters A, C, G, T, such that all words have the same number of letters in {C, G} (that number is free) and any two different words differ in at least 6 positions.
contract: construct() -> list of distinct strings of length 9 over the capital letters A, C, G, T (at least one word and at most 20000; a longer list is invalid). Score: number of words, maximized.
notes: Lower bound 54, not proven optimal: a code of that size was published on 2026-10-14 (https://github.com/owhs/DNA_GC_codes_2026) and passes this task's verifier. The table of Gaborit and King, last updated 23 June 2010, has 48 (construction 'v'). The tables of King and of Gaborit and King are for GC-content w = floor(n/2) (King 2003, section 'Tables': 'with d <= n and w = n/2'; Chee and Ling 2008, section V: 'lower bounds on A4GC,RC(n, d, floor(n/2)), the size of DNA codes having 50% GC-content'). This task lets the code choose any one constant w, a relaxation of the tabulated problem: a table value stays reachable with w = floor(n/2), and a larger code with another w improves this task's record but not the table entry (until 2026-11-18 the task fixed w = floor(n/2), which put four records of Aboluion et al. out of reach).
Entry A4GC(9,6) of the Gaborit-King table of lower bounds for DNA codes of length 9, GC-content 4 and minimum Hamming distance 6.

The record is a code from a 2026 repository, found by an automated search and not published in a paper; it was replayed word by word through this task's verifier. Papers published after 2014 were not searched systematically.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a DNA code of length 9 (words over A, C, G, T with exactly floor(9/2) letters from C and G, pairwise Hamming distance at least 6) with as many words as possible.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Such word sets serve as barcodes, microarray probes and tags in DNA computing and storage, where words must not hybridise with each other; a constant GC-content gives similar melting temperatures and a large Hamming distance makes mismatched pairing unlikely. The maximum size is unknown for almost all parameters and the pinned table has been the reference for lower bounds since 2010, so a larger code is a new lower bound.

papers.title: Bounds for DNA Codes with Constant GC-Content
papers.task_relation: The paper defines the quantity the task maximises for length 9 and distance 6 (GC-content floor(9/2)); its lexicographic constructions and Johnson-type bounds underlie the table the task starts from. The task covers the plain constant-GC variant.
papers.primary_goal: Derive upper and lower bounds on the maximum size of DNA codes with constant GC-content and minimum Hamming distance, with and without the reverse-complement constraint, and construct larger codes than previously published.

papers.title: Linear constructions for DNA codes
papers.task_relation: Its constructions give many entries of the table for length 9 and distance 6 (superscripts c, l and m on the pinned page); the task asks to beat the tabulated size. Covers the plain constant-GC variant.
papers.primary_goal: Construct DNA codes with constant GC-content from linear and related codes and tabulate the resulting lower bounds.

papers.title: Improved Lower Bounds for Constant GC-Content DNA Codes
papers.task_relation: Supplies table entries marked a, b and colon-optimal on the pinned page; the task asks for a larger code than the tabulated one for length 9, distance 6.
papers.primary_goal: Improve the lower bounds on the size of constant GC-content DNA codes, with and without the reverse-complement constraint, by stochastic local search, and prove some entries optimal by clique computations.
